model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) percentage of different models as a function of the co-occurrence number. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and ranges from 40% to 65%. The plot includes six lines, each representing a different model: Base (black line with circle markers), MEND (brown line with diamond markers), FT (blue line with triangle markers), MEMIT (purple line with pentagon markers), IKE (red line with square markers), and ROME (green line with cross markers). The Base model starts at approximately 40% accuracy at the lowest co-occurrence number and ends at about 45% at the highest co-occurrence number. MEND starts at around 45% and ends at about 55%. FT begins at approximately 40% and ends at about 50%. MEMIT starts at around 50% and ends at about 60%. IKE begins at about 45% and ends at around 50%. Lastly, ROME starts at approximately 50% and ends at about 65%. The plot shows a general trend of increasing accuracy with the increase in co-occurrence number for all models, with ROME showing the highest accuracy at the highest co-occurrence number.
